problem: Zero-shot object navigation methods ignore high-dimensional implicit scene information (object-room correlations, area adjacency) and suffer circuitous paths in long-range search, since they rely on local perception or lossy text conversion of the scene.
motivation: Human spaces have regular functional zoning (kitchen-utensils, bedroom-bathroom adjacency) that can guide exploration if fused across frames and extended to unobserved areas. An MLLM decision-maker working on an abstracted attribute map could avoid both history loss and redundant information.
key_idea: Build an Environmental Attributes Map (SBERT-reasoned room attributes for observed areas plus diffusion-inpainted floor-plan prediction for unobserved areas) and let a multimodal LLM hierarchically pick frontiers and objects on it.
insight: Ablations show both parts matter: replacing the SBERT-based EAM with LLM-EAM or GLIP-EAM lowers SR/SPL (33.1/16.2 and 36.5/22.7 vs 43.1/28.4). Replacing MHR with a text-only LLM (35.6/18.5) or random frontier choice (32.2/14.1, about Frontier level) shows that feeding spatial attribute maps to the MLLM is what gives the gain. Fine-tuning SBERT on HM3D/MP3D object-room triplets raises scene understanding consistency (MP3D 47.1 to 64.5).
method: Diffusion floor-plan inpainting: Stable Diffusion 1.5 fine-tuned with LoRA (rank 32) on RPLAN floor plans, with partial VAE fine-tuning, to complete unobserved regions from partial observations via masked iterative inpainting
EAM construction: RGB-D projected to a point cloud; low points form the exploration/occupancy layer, high points form room structure constraints; a zero-shot detector gives an object list per frame

SBERT scene reasoning: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 fine-tuned with triplet/MultipleNegativesRanking loss on HM3D/MP3D object-description to room-class data (15 classes) classifies each frame's primary environment
Attribute propagation: room attribute embeddings are diffused over 8-connected free neighbours with geometry-derived weights to fill a 3-layer grid map (object, environment attribute, exploration)

MHR module: Doubao-vision-pro-32k performs three-level reasoning (commonsense: which room type likely holds the target; environment: choose frontier on EAM image; object: local search in the target room)
TSP planning: frontier and object waypoints are ordered by a TSP solver and local waypoints sampled along the path to reduce LLM latency

setting.backbone: Doubao-vision-pro-32k (frozen MLLM) + fine-tuned SBERT (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) + LoRA-fine-tuned Stable Diffusion 1.5 + zero-shot detector (GLIP-like, unspecified)
setting.training_data: Diffusion: RPLAN floor plans (50,000 train); SBERT: object-room triplets collected from HM3D and MP3D training scenes; MLLM zero-shot
setting.action_space: frontier/waypoint selection converted to local navigation (Habitat)
setting.privileged: none at test time (HM3D/MP3D room annotations used only to build SBERT training data)

numbers.extra: long-range episodes only; diffusion and SBERT fine-tuned

numbers_note: Split names are not stated in the paper; 'val' is assumed. The text has inconsistent claims: ESC SPL 22.3 in the table vs 21.5 in text, and abstract improvements of 21.4%/46.0% do not match the tables. Component validation (SUC/EPP) is in a separate table: HM3D 51.1/35.2, MP3D 64.5/36.2.
results: On long-range HM3D and MP3D episodes, the method reaches SR 43.1/41.2 and SPL 28.4/26.3, beating ESC (39.2/22.3 HM3D; 28.7/14.2 MP3D) and Frontier (33.7/15.3; 36.0/17.7). Fine-tuning improves SBERT scene understanding consistency and effective prediction percentage.
limitations: Performance degrades in non-standard spaces without clear functional zoning (e.g., studio apartments)
Only two weak baselines (Frontier, ESC), a small evaluation, and unclear splits and episode counts; the diffusion predictor is trained on East Asian RPLAN floor plans, and no ablation isolates it
No real-robot experiments; relies on a closed-source MLLM with latency
